subject.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro: textSignature bloat + think tags + mixed text/tool causes session failures

question: For same-route Google Gemini replay, should OpenClaw keep valid Gemini text/thought signatures in persisted session history, strip them from history, or move them into a bounded replay-owned store/metadata shape?
rationale: Google's current contract makes signatures relevant for multi-turn reasoning continuity, while this issue shows that retaining them verbatim can bloat session history and break compaction/delivery, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Bound retained signatures
options.body: Keep only the minimum required same-route Gemini signatures in a bounded canonical replay store or compact metadata shape and strip large opaque values from ordinary session history.

options.title: Strip signatures from history
options.body: Drop Gemini text/thought signatures during persistence or replay to eliminate bloat, accepting possible loss of provider reasoning/tool-call continuity.

options.title: Keep validation-only behavior
options.body: Treat malformed-signature validation and native reasoning as sufficient and accept valid signature growth as a provider cost.

recommendation.title: Bound retained signatures
recommendation.body: Keep only the minimum required same-route Gemini signatures in a bounded canonical replay store or compact metadata shape and strip large opaque values from ordinary session history.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged transport validation work is the closest history signal for the remaining Gemini signature replay contract.
